chunks.text:
# IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ

Source: https://bob.ibm.com/docs/

## What is IBM Bob?

IBM Bob is an AI SDLC (Software Development Lifecycle) partner that augments your existing workflows and helps you understand, plan, improve, and work confidently with real codebases—while offering proactive insights that keep you in control every step.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.text:
IBM Bob is an **agentic integrated development environment (IDE)** that helps you write, test, upgrade, and secure software across the entire software development lifecycle (SDLC).

## How does Bob work?

Bob uses large language models (LLMs) to understand your requests and translate them into actions. It can:

- Read and write files in your project.
- Execute commands in your terminal.
- Perform web browsing (if enabled).
- Use external tools via the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.text:
You interact with Bob through a chat interface, where you provide instructions and review/approve its proposed actions.

## What can Bob do?

Bob can help with a variety of coding tasks, including:

- Generating code from natural language descriptions.
- Refactoring existing code.
- Fixing bugs.
- Writing documentation.
- Explaining code.
- Answering questions about your codebase.
- Automating repetitive tasks.
- Creating new files and projects.

## Can I use Bob on my IBM code?

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.text:
Bob has been approved for use on **all IBM product codebases**.

## Are there any restrictions on processing certain data types with Bob?

The following data types should **not** be processed with Bob:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.text:
- SPI (Sensitive Personal Information)
- Personal Health Information (PHI)
- Export control code that are marked as 'Red' or 'Gray' (i.e., export-controlled code up to Orange zone is permitted)
- Non-IBM IP (Open source is allowed, but review the license first and remove any Bob tags)
- Sensitive Financial Data (banking numbers, PANs, credit card numbers)
- Material Non-Public Information (MNPI), such as financial data that has not been made public

## Can I choose which model Bob uses?

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.text:
No. Bob **automatically selects** the most appropriate language model for each task based on complexity, required capabilities, and cost-efficiency. This intelligent routing ensures you receive high-quality responses while optimizing resource usage.

Bob's model selection considers:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.text:
- **Task complexity** — Simple tasks use faster, more cost-effective models.
- **Required capabilities** — Specialized tasks route to models with specific strengths.
- **Context size** — Large codebases may require models with extended context windows.
- **Cost optimization** — Balances performance with efficient resource usage.

## Getting Started with Bob IDE

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.text:
1. **Install Bob** — Get Bob installed on your system. See [Installing Bob](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/getting-started/install).
2. **Learn best practices** — Review the best practices guide. See [Best practices for using Bob](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/getting-started/best-practices).
3. **Review security guidelines** — Consult the security guidelines. See [Security guidelines](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/security/bob-security-guidance).

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob — Overview and General FAQ
chunks.text: **Tip:** Start with something you are currently working on. Bob learns best when helping with real problems rather than hypothetical scenarios.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Shell
chunks.text: # IBM Bob Shell Source: https://bob.ibm.com/docs/shell/ ## What is Bob Shell? Bob Shell brings IBM Bob's AI capabilities to your command line. As a terminal-based interface, Bob Shell provides AI-assistance for command-line tasks, script automation, and terminal-based workflows. Bob Shell delivers the same context awareness and reasoning-focused approach from IBM Bob, but **optimized for shell environments and automated processes**. ## What you can do with Bob Shell

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Shell
chunks.text:
- **Automate scripts** — Generate and optimize shell scripts for complex automation tasks.
- **Execute commands** — Run terminal commands with AI-powered assistance and validation.
- **Generate documentation** — Create comprehensive documentation for scripts and workflows.
- **Troubleshoot issues** — Debug command failures and resolve terminal-based problems.
- **Analyze logs** — Parse and analyze log files to identify issues and patterns.
- **Scaffold projects** — Initialize new projects and generate boilerplate code from the terminal.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Shell
chunks.text:
## Key capabilities

### Flexible ways to run Bob Shell

Bob Shell adapts to your workflow with flexible ways to work:

- **Interactive sessions** — Engage in conversational sessions directly in your terminal.
- **Non-interactive sessions** — Run commands or tasks for automation and scripting.
- **Automation support** — Seamlessly integrate into automated processes and workflows.
- **Editor terminal support** — Run Bob Shell inside terminal views of supported editors.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Shell
chunks.text:
Use interactive sessions for exploratory tasks and problem-solving. Switch to non-interactive sessions when you need to automate repetitive workflows or integrate Bob into scripts.

### Powerful command-line tools

Bob Shell provides comprehensive tools designed for terminal environments:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Shell
chunks.text:
- **File operations** — Read, write, and manipulate files directly from the command line.
- **Running commands** — Run shell commands with intelligent error handling and validation.
- **Process management** — Monitor and control running processes and system resources.
- **External tools with MCP** — Connect to external services via the Model Context Protocol.

### Custom modes and slash commands

Extend Bob Shell's functionality with custom modes and slash commands:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Shell
chunks.text:
- Define custom modes for specialized workflows.
- Create reusable command shortcuts.
- Build team-specific automation patterns.
- Standardize development processes across your organization.

### MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration

MCP extends Bob Shell's capabilities with custom tools tailored for command-line workflows:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Shell
chunks.text:
- Connect to databases and APIs from the terminal.
- Access specialized development and operations tools.
- Integrate with your organization's internal systems.
- Create custom automation workflows for DevOps tasks.

## Getting started with Bob Shell

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Shell
chunks.text:
1. Install Bob Shell on your system. See [Installing and setting up Bob Shell](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/shell/getting-started/install-and-setup).
2. Launch your first interactive session. See [Starting Bob Shell interactively](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/shell/getting-started/start-bobshell-interactive).
3. Review the security guidelines to minimize potential security risks. See [Security guidelines](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/security/bob-security-guidance).

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Shell
chunks.text:
**Note:** Start by using Bob Shell for a task you're already familiar with.

## Using slash commands

Type `/` to access a menu of available commands:

- Built-in commands like `/help` for assistance.
- Mode-switching commands like `/code` or `/ask`.
- Custom commands you've created.

For a complete list, see [Slash commands in Bob Shell](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/shell/features/slash-commands).

## FAQ — Bob Shell

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Shell
chunks.text:
**What is MCP (Model Context Protocol)?**
MCP is a protocol that allows Bob to communicate with external servers, extending its capabilities with custom tools and resources.

**Can I create my own MCP servers?**
Yes. You can create your own MCP servers to add custom functionality to Bob. See [Using MCP in Bob](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/configuration/mcp/mcp-in-bob).

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Enterprise Plan
chunks.text:
# IBM Bob Enterprise Plan

Source: https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/enterprise/

## Overview

Scale IBM Bob across your organization with centralized control. IBM Bob Enterprise provides enhanced team management capabilities, shared Bobcoin allocation, and dedicated support to help your organization maximize productivity.

### Key Enterprise Features

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Enterprise Plan
chunks.text:
- **Shared Bobcoin pool** — Distribute Bobcoins from a centralized budget to empower your entire team.
- **Admin dashboard** — Control spending, manage users, and track usage across your organization.
- **Enterprise support** — Get assistance from dedicated IBM Bob specialists.
- **Scale on demand** — Purchase additional Bobcoin packs as your team grows.
- **Bobalytics** — Analytics and insights into team adoption (Enterprise only).

## Centralized Management

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Enterprise Plan
chunks.text:
The administration dashboard provides:

- **Shared Bobcoin pool** — Distribute Bobcoins to team members.
- **User management** — Use Seats to add, remove, and manage team member access.
- **Spending controls** — Set individual spending limits and adjust based on your team needs.
- **Usage insights** — Monitor Bobcoin consumption and optimize your resource allocation.

Your IBM Bob Enterprise plan provides access to the [Administration](https://bob.ibm.com/admin) page.

## User Roles

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Enterprise Plan
chunks.text:
IBM Bob Enterprise provides two role types:

- **User** — Can access IBM Bob and use AI features within their assigned team's spending limits.
- **Admin** — Has all User permissions plus the ability to manage users, create and configure teams, and access the administration dashboard.

## Managing Users

Add users to your IBM Bob Enterprise organization, assign roles, manage seat allocation, and assign premium packages.

### Adding a User

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Enterprise Plan
chunks.text:
1. Go to the [IBM Bob Administration](https://bob.ibm.com/admin) page.
2. Go to **Users & Teams** and select the **Users** tab.

### Assigning a Premium Package to a User

1. Go to the [IBM Bob Administration](https://bob.ibm.com/admin) page.
2. Go to **Users & Teams** and select the **Users** tab.
3. Select the user you want to update.
4. Under **Premium packages**, select the premium package to assign.

The user can access the premium package immediately after assignment.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Enterprise Plan
chunks.text:
### Removing a Premium Package from a User

1. Go to the [IBM Bob Administration](https://bob.ibm.com/admin) page.
2. Go to **Users & Teams** and select the **Users** tab.
3. Select the user you want to update.
4. Under **Premium packages**, deselect the premium package to remove.

**Note:** Premium package entitlements are time-bound. Each assigned package displays its active period and expiry date in the user's add-on list.

### Viewing Add-on Seat Usage

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Enterprise Plan
chunks.text:
The **Add-ons** summary in the admin UI shows each premium package with its purchased seat count and how many are currently assigned.

## Support

Enterprise customers get access to dedicated assistance from IBM Bob specialists. You can open a support case on the [IBM Support](https://www.ibm.com/mysupport/s/?language=en_US) website.

## Managing Your Subscription

To manage your IBM Bob Enterprise plan, including upgrades, downgrades, or billing changes, contact your IBM Sales representative.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Premium Packages
chunks.text:
# IBM Bob Premium Packages

Source: https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/premium-packages/

## Overview

Premium packages are **optional add-ons** that extend IBM Bob with specialized capabilities. They are available exclusively on the IBM Bob Enterprise plan.

Admins can:
- View how many seats have been purchased and assigned for each package.
- Control which users have access.

## Managing Premium Packages

### Assigning a Premium Package to a User

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Premium Packages
chunks.text:
1. Go to the [IBM Bob Administration](https://bob.ibm.com/admin) page.
2. Go to **Users & Teams** and select the **Users** tab.
3. Select the user you want to update.
4. Under **Premium packages**, select the premium package to assign.

The user can access the premium package immediately after assignment.

### Removing a Premium Package from a User

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Premium Packages
chunks.text:
1. Go to the [IBM Bob Administration](https://bob.ibm.com/admin) page.
2. Go to **Users & Teams** and select the **Users** tab.
3. Select the user you want to update.
4. Under **Premium packages**, deselect the premium package to remove.

**Note:** Premium package entitlements are time-bound. Each assigned package displays its active period and expiry date in the user's add-on list.

### Viewing Add-on Seat Usage

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Premium Packages
chunks.text:
The **Add-ons** summary in the admin UI shows each premium package with:
- Purchased seat count.
- Number of seats currently assigned.

Use this to track availability before assigning packages to users.

## Further Information

For more information, see [Premium packages overview](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/premium-packages/pkg-index).

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Skills
chunks.text:
# IBM Bob Skills

Source: https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/features/skills

## What are Skills?

Skills are **reusable instruction sets** that teach Bob new workflows and specialized tasks. Think of them as recipes that Bob follows to complete specific types of work in a consistent, repeatable manner.

## How Skills Work

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Skills
chunks.text:
When you activate a skill, Bob receives the skill's instructions and gains access to any supporting files in the skill directory. Bob then follows these instructions to complete your task according to the defined workflow.

Skills load **once per conversation** to avoid duplicate prompts. Bob automatically determines when to activate a skill based on your request and the skill's description.

## Creating a Skill

### Basic Setup

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Skills
chunks.text:
1. Create a folder inside `.bob/skills/` in your project root, or use `~/.bob/skills/` for global skills.
2. Add a `SKILL.md` file inside that folder.

**Example structure:**
```
your-project/
└── .bob/
    └── skills/
        └── code-review/
            └── SKILL.md
```

### SKILL.md Format

The `SKILL.md` file uses YAML front matter followed by the skill instructions:

```markdown
---
name: code-review
description: Review code for bugs, security issues, and best practices
---

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Skills
chunks.text:
When reviewing code, check for:
- Security vulnerabilities
- Performance issues
- Missing error handling at API boundaries
- Unused imports and dead code

Provide a summary with severity levels for each finding.
```

**Required fields:**
- `name` — The skill's display name used in the Bob interface.
- `description` — A clear summary that helps Bob decide when to activate this skill. Skills without descriptions are ignored.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Skills
chunks.text:
**Instructions section:** Everything below the `---` delimiter becomes the instructions Bob receives when the skill is activated.

## Adding Supporting Files

You can include additional files and subfolders alongside `SKILL.md` to provide reference materials, templates, checklists, scripts, or other resources. Bob can read these files automatically once the skill is activated.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Skills
chunks.text:
**Example with supporting files:**
```
.bob/skills/
└── code-review/
    ├── SKILL.md
    ├── checklist.md
    ├── severity-guide.md
    └── scripts/
        ├── analyze.sh
        └── report-generator.py
```

Supporting files can include:
- Checklists and templates
- Reference documentation
- Configuration examples
- Scripts and utilities in subfolders
- Style guides

## Skill Locations

Skills can be defined at two levels:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Skills
chunks.text:
- `<project>/.bob/skills/` — Project-specific; used for workflows unique to this project.
- `~/.bob/skills/` — Global; used for personal or organization-wide workflows.

**Priority:** If both locations contain a skill with the same name, the project-level skill takes precedence.

## Approving Skills

By default, Bob asks for your permission before activating a skill.

To skip the approval prompt:
1. Open Bob Settings.
2. Navigate to the Auto-Approve section.
3. Turn on the toggle for **Skills**.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Skills
chunks.text: With this setting enabled, Bob automatically activates skills when appropriate without requesting permission.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.text:
# IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol

Source: https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/configuration/mcp/

## What is MCP?

The **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** extends Bob's capabilities by connecting to external tools and services. MCP allows Bob to communicate with external servers, extending its capabilities with custom tools and resources.

An MCP server acts as a bridge between Bob and external services like databases, APIs, or custom scripts.

MCP servers provide Bob with:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.text:
- **Tool discovery** — Access to available tools with their descriptions and parameters.
- **Tool invocation** — The ability to call specific tools with arguments and receive structured responses.
- **Resource access** — The capability to read data from specific resources.

## Why Use MCP?

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.text:
- **Extend functionality** — Add custom capabilities to Bob that aren't available out-of-the-box.
- **Integrate with services** — Connect Bob to your databases, APIs, and other systems.
- **Automate workflows** — Create specialized tools for your specific needs.
- **Share capabilities** — Distribute useful tools across your team.

## MCP in Bob IDE

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) extends Bob's capabilities with custom tools and integrations:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.text:
- **Understanding MCP** — Learn how MCP works and its role in extending Bob's capabilities.
- **Server transports** — Choose between local and remote deployment models for your MCP servers.
- **MCP server management** — Add, configure, and remove MCP servers directly from the settings panel.

For more information, see [Using MCP in Bob](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/configuration/mcp/mcp-in-bob).

## MCP in Bob Shell

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.text:
Bob Shell supports MCP, allowing you to extend Bob's capabilities by connecting to external services and tools:

- Connect to databases and APIs from the terminal.
- Access specialized development and operations tools.
- Integrate with your organization's internal systems.
- Create custom automation workflows for DevOps tasks.

For more information, see [MCP in Bob Shell](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/shell/configuration/mcp/mcp-bobshell).

## Using MCP Securely

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.text:
Model Context Protocol extends Bob's functionality by connecting to external tools and services. While powerful, MCP connections require careful security consideration.

When using MCP servers, follow these guidelines:

- **Authentication** — Verify the identity of users accessing the server.
- **Encryption** — Secure data in transit between Bob and the server.
- **Access controls** — Limit what actions the server can perform.
- **Auditing** — Track all actions for accountability.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.text:
Remote MCP servers must adhere to the same security requirements as any traditional server infrastructure, including endpoint protection, network restrictions, and proper access controls.

For shared MCP servers, ensure proper auditability and accountability so actions can be traced.

## Auto-Approve for MCP

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob MCP — Model Context Protocol
chunks.text:
Bob can use configured MCP servers without asking permission if auto-approve is enabled for MCP. The risk level depends on what the specific MCP servers can access and modify. Use with caution.

## FAQ

**Can I create my own MCP servers?**
Yes. You can create your own MCP servers to add custom functionality to Bob. See [Using MCP in Bob](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/configuration/mcp/mcp-in-bob).

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Security Guidelines
chunks.text:
# IBM Bob Security Guidelines

Source: https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/security/bob-security-guidance

## Overview

Bob is an AI coding assistant designed to help IBMers write secure, maintainable code. This document defines mandatory security standards that MUST be followed in all code suggestions, architecture recommendations, and technical guidance.

## Data Restrictions

The following data types should **not** be processed with Bob:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Security Guidelines
chunks.text:
- SPI (Sensitive Personal Information)
- Personal Health Information (PHI)
- Export control code marked as 'Red' or 'Gray'
- Non-IBM IP (Open source is allowed, but review the license first)
- Sensitive Financial Data (banking numbers, PANs, credit card numbers)
- Material Non-Public Information (MNPI)

## Security Hardening

You can apply additional security rules to Bob by creating custom rules files. These are stored in `.bob/rules/` or `.bob/rules-{mode-slug}/` directories.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Security Guidelines
chunks.text:
See [Custom rules](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/configuration/rules) and [Security hardening](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/security/security-hardening) for more information.

## Auto-Approve Settings

With Bob, you can automatically approve various actions without confirmation prompts. While this speeds up your workflow, it significantly increases security risks.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Security Guidelines
chunks.text:
**Warning:** Auto-approve settings bypass confirmation prompts, giving Bob direct access to your system. This can result in **data loss, file corruption, or worse**. Command line access is particularly dangerous, as it can potentially run harmful operations.

Configure auto-approval with care:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Security Guidelines
chunks.text:
- **Manual approval** — Review and approve every action Bob takes (safest setting).
- **Auto-approve** — Grant Bob the ability to run specific tasks without interruption.
- **Hybrid approach** — Auto-approve low-risk actions while requiring confirmation for riskier tasks.

## Using .bobignore

The `.bobignore` file lets you specify files and directories that Bob should not access or modify:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Security Guidelines
chunks.text:
1. Create a `.bobignore` file in your project root.
2. Add patterns for sensitive files, build artifacts, and large assets.
3. Use the same syntax as `.gitignore`.

This helps protect sensitive information and prevent accidental changes to generated files.

See [Using .bobignore](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/configuration/bobignore) for more information.

## Using MCP Securely

When using MCP servers:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Security Guidelines
chunks.text:
- **Authentication** — Verify the identity of users accessing the server.
- **Encryption** — Secure data in transit between Bob and the server.
- **Access controls** — Limit what actions the server can perform.
- **Auditing** — Track all actions for accountability.

Remote MCP servers must adhere to the same security requirements as any traditional server infrastructure.

## Proxy Configuration

For enterprise environments with network restrictions, configure proxy settings for IBM Bob IDE.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Security Guidelines
chunks.text: See [Configuring proxy settings](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/troubleshooting/ts-proxy) for more information.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Telemetry
chunks.text:
# IBM Bob Telemetry

Source: https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/configuration/telemetry-data

## IBM Bob IDE Telemetry

IBM Bob collects telemetry data **by default** to help improve the product. You can opt out to disable telemetry data collection at any time.

**Note:** Enterprise plan users must keep telemetry enabled to view data in Bobalytics. Disabling telemetry will prevent your usage data from appearing in analytics dashboards.

### What data is collected?

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Telemetry
chunks.text:
When telemetry is enabled, IBM Bob collects:

- Actions you take in IBM Bob.
- Features you use and how they perform.
- Error and diagnostic information.

**Privacy:** IBM Bob does **not** collect your code, prompts, or other sensitive information as part of telemetry data.

### How is the data used?

This data helps IBM:

- Identify which features are most useful to users.
- Prioritize future development efforts.
- Diagnose and fix issues.
- Improve overall product quality.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Telemetry
chunks.text:
### How to configure telemetry

1. Click the settings gear icon in the Bob panel.
2. Select the **General** tab.
3. Toggle **Telemetry** on or off.

## Bob Shell Telemetry

IBM Bob does **not** collect telemetry data by default in Bob Shell. You must **opt in** to enable telemetry data collection.

When enabled in Bob Shell:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Telemetry
chunks.text:
- Actions are recorded that you take in IBM Bob.
- It helps identify which features are the most useful to users.
- You can enable or disable the collection of this data at any time.

### Collected data categories

Bob Shell telemetry can collect:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Telemetry
chunks.text:
- Records the action of a task being opened, completed, or reopened.
- Records the generation, acceptance, or rejection of inline code completion.
- Records the initiation, successful completion, or failure of a scheduled scan.
- Records confirmation, clarification, or approval of tasks.
- Records the action of a message being sent from you to Bob or Bob to you.
- Records the use of tool invocations, such as `execute_command`, `read_file`, and others.

### Opting out of Bob Shell usage statistics

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Telemetry
IBM Bob — IBM Bob Modes (Built-in and Custom)
chunks.text:
# IBM Bob Modes (Built-in and Custom)

Source: https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/features/modes

## What are Modes?

Modes are **specialized personas** that tailor Bob's behavior for your specific tasks. Each mode offers different capabilities and access levels to help you accomplish particular goals more efficiently.

## Built-in Modes

Bob ships with several built-in modes:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Modes (Built-in and Custom)
chunks.text:
- **Code** — For implementation tasks, writing and editing code.
- **Plan** — For architecture design and planning features before implementation.
- **Ask** — For asking questions about your codebase without making changes.
- **Advanced** — For more complex, multi-step tasks.
- **Orchestrator** — For coordinating multiple agents and tools.

## Custom Modes

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Modes (Built-in and Custom)
chunks.text:
Custom modes extend modes by letting teams and developers define specialized personas with tailored instructions and specific tool access. A custom mode combines:

- A **role definition** — what Bob is in this mode.
- **Behavioral instructions** — how Bob acts in this mode.
- A **deterministic set of permitted tools** — what tools Bob can use.

**Rules** apply to every conversation regardless of mode. A custom mode does not override or bypass rules.

### Creating a Custom Mode

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Modes (Built-in and Custom)
chunks.text:
You can override default Bob modes (such as Agent, Ask, or Plan) by creating a custom mode with the same slug in your project configuration.

**To create or edit custom modes:**

1. Click the Settings icon in the Bob panel to open Settings.
2. Select the **Modes** tab.
3. Click **Edit Project Modes** to edit the `.bob/custom_modes.yaml` file.
4. Add your mode configuration:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Modes (Built-in and Custom)
chunks.text:
```yaml
customModes:
  - slug: ask  # Matches default Ask mode
    name: ❓ Ask
    roleDefinition: You are a knowledgeable assistant for this React and TypeScript codebase.
    whenToUse: Use this mode to ask questions about the codebase.
    customInstructions: Always reference relevant files when answering.
    groups:
      - read
      - mcp
      - skill
```

**Priority:** Project-specific overrides take precedence over global overrides, which take precedence over defaults.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Modes (Built-in and Custom)
chunks.text:
## Custom Modes in Bob Shell

Custom modes in Bob Shell work similarly to Bob IDE modes. The key properties are:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Modes (Built-in and Custom)
chunks.text:
- `slug` — Unique internal identifier; used in command-line arguments (e.g., `bob --chat-mode=my-mode`).
- `name` — Display name in the UI.
- `description` — Short description shown in the mode selector.
- `roleDefinition` — Defines the core identity and expertise.
- `groups` — Specifies allowed toolsets and file access.
- `whenToUse` — Mode selection guidance.
- `customInstructions` — Specific behavioral guidelines or rules for the mode.

## Mode Switching

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Modes (Built-in and Custom)
chunks.text:
- In the IDE: Use the mode selector in the Bob panel.
- In Bob Shell: Use slash commands (e.g., `/mode code`, `/mode ask`).
- Custom modes appear as slash commands (e.g., a mode with slug `reviewer` becomes `/reviewer`).

## Further Information

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Modes (Built-in and Custom)
chunks.text:
- [Custom modes documentation](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/configuration/custom-modes)
- [Custom modes in Bob Shell](https://bob.ibm.com/docs/shell/configuration/custom-modes-bobshell)

chunks.text:
# IBM Bob Bobcoins — Usage and Budget

Source: https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/account/bobcoins

## What are Bobcoins?

Bobcoins are IBM Bob's usage metric that convert token usage into a **predictable budget system**. One Bobcoin represents a standardized amount of computational resources, including token usage across different models and operations.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Bobcoins — Usage and Budget
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob Bobcoins — Usage and Budget
chunks.text:
You don't need to track tokens directly—IBM Bob automatically converts your model usage into Bobcoins. Different models and operations consume tokens at different rates, but Bobcoins provide a consistent way to understand and manage your usage.

## Bobcoins vs. Tokens

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Bobcoins — Usage and Budget
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob Bobcoins — Usage and Budget
chunks.text:
- **Tokens** — Raw units of model usage representing pieces of text (words, characters) that the AI model processes. Every request consumes input tokens (your prompt and context) and output tokens (Bob's response).
- **Bobcoins** — IBM Bob's usage metric. Converts token usage into a predictable budget system.

## Monthly Budget

Your Bobcoin budget determines how much you can use IBM Bob each month.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Bobcoins — Usage and Budget
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob Bobcoins — Usage and Budget
chunks.text:
- **Budget resets** on a specific day each month (check the Settings panel to see your reset date).
- **Unused Bobcoins do not carry forward** to the next month.
- Your balance resets to your monthly allocated amount (based on your tier).

## Budget Tier Progression

You can permanently increase your monthly Bobcoin allocation by providing feedback:

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Bobcoins — Usage and Budget
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob Bobcoins — Usage and Budget
chunks.text:
| Tier | Monthly Bobcoins | How to reach |
|------|-----------------|--------------|
| Tier 1 | 500 | Default starting tier |
| Tier 2 | 750 | Submit the first feedback |
| Tier 3 | 1000 | Submit the second feedback |
| Tier 4 | 2000 | Submit the third feedback |

**Example:** If you submit feedback twice and reach tier 3, you will start every month with 1000 Bobcoins.

**Note:** If you have less than 500 Bobcoins, you must use the feedback system when prompted to get updated to the tier 1 amount.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Bobcoins — Usage and Budget
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob Bobcoins — Usage and Budget
chunks.text:
## Monitoring Your Usage You can track your Bobcoin usage in two ways: 1. **Budget gauge** — Hover your cursor over the gauge component in the top-right corner of the Bob panel to see your remaining balance.
2. **Chat interface** — When a conversation is open, view your token and Bobcoin usage in the top-right corner of the chat interface. ## Managing Your Budget Effectively

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Bobcoins — Usage and Budget
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob Bobcoins — Usage and Budget
chunks.text:
- **Provide feedback early** — Submit feedback when prompted to increase your budget tier before running out.
- **Monitor your usage regularly** — Keep track of your Bobcoin balance to plan your work.
- **Use only required context** — Start new chats when the task changes to avoid carrying over irrelevant context.
- **Limit MCP server use** — Excessive use of MCP servers can significantly increase Bobcoin consumption.
- **Share meaningful feedback** — Quality feedback helps improve IBM Bob and increases your budget.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Bobcoins — Usage and Budget
chunks.section_header: IBM Bob Bobcoins — Usage and Budget
chunks.text:
## Enterprise Bobcoins

On the Enterprise plan, Bobcoins are managed through a **shared pool**:

- Distribute Bobcoins from a centralized budget to empower your entire team.
- Admins can set individual spending limits.
- Purchase additional Bobcoin packs as your team grows.
- Monitor Bobcoin consumption through the admin dashboard.

chunks.text:
# IBM Bob Bobalytics — Analytics Dashboard

Source: https://bob.ibm.com/docs/ide/features/bobalytics

## What is Bobalytics?

Bobalytics provides **analytics and insights** into how IBM Bob contributes to your software development process. Use it to:

- Understand Bob's impact on your codebase.
- Track Bobcoin spending.
- Monitor team adoption across your organization.

**Note:** Bobalytics is available **exclusively for Enterprise plan users**.

## Accessing Bobalytics

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Bobalytics — Analytics Dashboard
chunks.text:
1. Go to [bob.ibm.com](https://bob.ibm.com) and log in.
2. Click **Admin**, then select the **Bobalytics** tab.

## Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Bobalytics is organized around three KPIs:

### 1. Adoption Rate

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Bobalytics — Analytics Dashboard
chunks.text:
Adoption rate measures how consistently your team uses Bob. It is calculated as the average number of daily active users divided by the total number of licensed seats. A user is counted as active on a given day when they accept at least one code completion or complete a chat conversation.

**Primary metrics:**
- Team onboarding: adoption percentage for specific teams.
- Daily active users: a chart of active users over time.
- Team details and trends: Adoption, value, and cost metrics.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Bobalytics — Analytics Dashboard
chunks.text:
**Supporting metrics:**
- Usage levels: breakdown of users by how often they use Bob (multiple times per day, daily, weekly, occasional, or inactive).
- Bob's repository impact: repositories where Bob users have been most active.

**Tip:** If adoption rate is low, check usage levels to identify inactive or occasional users.

### 2. Bob Factor

Measures the value Bob brings to your software development process.

### 3. Bobcoin Spend

Tracks Bobcoin consumption across your organization.

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Bobalytics — Analytics Dashboard
chunks.text:
## Using Bobalytics Effectively

Check Bobalytics on a regular cadence — weekly or monthly — to spot trends:

- A **declining adoption rate** over several weeks may signal that users need additional enablement.
- A **sudden spike in Bobcoin spend** can be investigated by filtering down to a specific team or time range.
- A **steadily rising Bob factor** alongside stable spend is a strong signal that your team is getting increasing value from Bob.

## Telemetry Requirement

chunks.page_title: IBM Bob — IBM Bob Bobalytics — Analytics Dashboard
chunks.text: Enterprise plan users must keep telemetry enabled to view data in Bobalytics. Disabling telemetry will prevent your usage data from appearing in analytics dashboards.
